title: Criminal Code Amendment (Private Sexual Material) Bill 2015
short_title: Criminal Code Amendment (Private Sexual Material) Bill 2015

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would create three offences addressing non-consensual sharing of private sexual material, threats involving that material and preparation for those offences for commercial purposes or benefit.
The sharing and threat offences would carry maximum prison terms of three years, while the commercial or benefit-related preparatory offence would carry five years.
The changes would begin the day after Royal Assent, and prosecution of a person under 18 would require the Attorney-General’s consent under the proposed safeguards.
changes: The threat offence could apply even where the sexual material does not exist or the recipient does not actually fear the threat.
Sending the material to its subject would be excluded from the sharing offence.
Specified media activities would have a conditional defence to the sharing and preparatory offences, including a reasonable belief that the conduct serves the public interest.
summary.affected: People depicted in private sexual material, people sharing or threatening to share it and journalists would be affected.
